groups.title: Continuous Delivery Concepts
groups.question: Your team deploys a JAMstack site from Git, reviewers want to see changes before merge, and the site must rebuild when editors publish in the CMS. Explain how you would set up delivery.

followUps.Git-based deployments and trunk-based de: How do Git-based deployments and trunk-based development work together?
followUps.Deploy previews for pull request review: What does a deploy preview give reviewers?
followUps.Build hooks for triggering deploys from: How does a build hook connect the CMS to deploys?

evidence.text: Pushing to the configured branch deploys automatically.
Trunk-based development keeps main always deployable with short-lived branches.
Small, frequent merges keep each deploy low-risk.

notEnough: Only saying deploys happen on push.

evidence.text: Each pull request gets its own preview URL.
The preview runs the full build in an isolated environment.
Reviewers can test the real change before it is merged.
A build hook is a unique URL that starts a deploy when called.
The CMS calls it through a webhook when content is published.
The site is rebuilt with the new content automatically.

groups.title: Monitoring and Rollbacks
groups.question: A deploy broke the checkout page in production, and you only found out from a customer email. Explain how you would recover quickly and catch errors earlier.

followUps.Instant rollbacks to previous deploys on: How do instant rollbacks work on Netlify?
followUps.Error monitoring with Sentry for product: What does Sentry give you, and why upload source maps?

evidence.text: Netlify keeps every previous deploy.
You can restore an earlier deploy in one step.
That restores a working site in seconds while the bug is fixed.

notEnough: Only saying you can roll back.

evidence.text: Sentry captures errors from the browser and functions with stack traces and context.
It alerts you when errors happen, before users report them.
Source maps show the original code location instead of the minified one.

groups.title: Netlify Configuration and Build
groups.question: You are configuring Netlify so production uses the live CMS and previews use a staging one. Explain how the build is configured.

followUps.Managing build environment variables per: How can production and preview deploys use different environment values?

evidence.text: netlify.toml sets the build command and the folder to publish.
It can override settings per environment.
Build plugins add steps to the build, such as checks before or after it.
Netlify supports different variable values for production, previews and branch deploys.
Previews can point to a staging CMS environment.
This keeps test changes from touching production data.

notEnough: Only saying you set environment variables.

groups.title: Custom Domains and HTTPS
groups.question: You are moving your site to a custom domain with HTTPS and old URLs must keep working. Explain how you would set this up on Netlify.

followUps.Configuring a custom domain and automati: How does a custom domain get HTTPS on Netlify?
followUps.Netlify redirect rules and _redirects fi: How do you keep old URLs working after restructuring the site?

evidence.text: You add a DNS record that points the domain to Netlify.
Netlify automatically gets a free TLS certificate.
The certificate is renewed automatically.
A _redirects file maps old URLs to new ones.
Permanent moves use a 301 status so search engines update their index.
Wildcards and splats redirect whole sections in one rule.
